title: Handoff Harmony: Eviction and Transfer Playbook
author: Marissa Cheng
content:
Summary:

This playbook codifies a deterministic, observable approach for transferring in-flight requests and gracefully reclaiming runtime resources. It balances user-visible correctness (avoiding aborted responses and consistency loss) with operator needs for fast resource reclamation during scale events, maintenance, or kernel failures.

Audience:
- Runtime engineers
- SREs on-call for runtime clusters
- Platform owners planning canaries or capacity changes

Goals and guardrails:
- User-visible aborts from planned or forced handoffs should be < 0.05% monthly.
- Typical handoff commit latency: median <= 150 ms; p99 <= 2.5s for short requests.
- Eviction flows must reclaim a node within configured eviction_window while providing final best-effort completion for affected sessions.

Core terminology (short):
- handoff_token: single-use opaque identifier with expiry ISO8601 timestamp. Appears in traces.
- drain_epoch: the short wait after marking sessions to allow running kernels to finish naturally (configurable).
- eviction_window: hard timeout for completing a transfer or executing graceful eviction.
- kv-sync: optional asynchronous synchronization of minimal KV state to target. Marks session degraded if incomplete.
- preempt_credit: a small retry allowance given to callers during transfer to reduce client-visible failures.

Architecture components involved:
- runtime-dispatcher (dispatcher): selects destination node/shard and initiates handoff intents.
- node-agent: per-host service orchestrating local drain, KV exports, kernel lifecycle, and final commit/eviction actions.
- handoff-orchestrator (leader): optional distributed coordinator for multi-shard transfers and conflict resolution. Data store: etcd.
- telemetry-agent: annotates traces with handoff_token and emits events for Handoff:started, Handoff:committed, Handoff:evicted.

Protocol (ordered steps):
1) Dispatcher detects transfer reason: planned drain, OS maintenance, GPU error, preemption, or capacity balancing. It calculates candidate target(s) and issues an Intent to node-agent: {token, targets, reason, ttl}.
2) Node-agent marks sessions in drain set and enters drain_epoch. It sets internal state to DRAINING and begins non-blocking kv-sync for streaming sessions.
3) Handoff-orchestrator (if present) attempts to reserve a receive slot on the target node. Reservation response includes acceptance, backoff recommendation, or alternate node list.
4) Target node verifies compatibility (model variant, quantization profile, KV shard affinity) and responds. If accepted, it returns a receive_handle with a short TTL.
5) Source node streams session metadata and small KV chunks (if supported). Only metadata required to resume decoding is streamed; secrets and raw user payloads are never proxied.
6) Target node writes session metadata to local cache, acknowledges, and telemetry records Handoff:committed. Source node marks session COMPLETE_LOCAL_CLEANUP and releases kernel resources.
7) If the sequence fails to finish before eviction_window, node-agent triggers graceful-eviction: attempt a synthetic completion (fast-fallback generation), then issue final kernel teardown and emit Handoff:evicted.

Configuration reference (defaults):
| key | default | note |
| .handoff.eviction_window_secs | "30" | applies to short non-stream sessions |
| .handoff.stream_eviction_window_secs | "120" | applies to chat/stream sessions |
| .handoff.drain_epoch_ms | "1500" | small wait to let kernels finish naturally |
| .handoff.max_parallel_transfers | "6" | per-node outgoing transfer concurrency |
| .handoff.preempt_credit_tokens | "1" | number of ephemeral retries clients may consume |
| .handoff.kv_sync_enabled | "true" | best-effort; false disables KV transfer attempts |

Observed failure patterns and recommended mitigations:
- reservation_timeouts (common): when requests queue at dispatcher due to oversubscription. Actions: reduce dispatcher weight, scale dedicated capacity, or reroute to compatible fallback variant. Metric: handoff_reserve_timeout_total.
- kernel_stall during drain: identified by kernel.active_ms spikes and no progress markers. Action: extend drain_epoch up to a soft cap once for kernels flagged as idempotent; otherwise escalate to forced eviction. Metric: kernel_blocked_handoff_total.
- kv_sync_partial: KV sync completed partially. Action: mark session degraded; downstream resume will perform token re-priming. Metric: handoff_kv_partial_total.
- oscillation between nodes: rapid flip-flops identified by repeated commits for same session token. Action: insert randomized cooldown (2m) and raise handoff priority to avoid future oscillations.

Operational runbook (triage):
Alert triggers:
- handoff_reserve_timeout_rate > 5/min sustained for 3m
- handoff_evicted.rate spikes > 1/min for 5m
- handoff_kv_partial.rate > baseline by 200%

Initial responder steps (SRE):
1) Confirm alerts and scope: query Prometheus examples:
   - sum(rate(handoff_reserve_timeout_total[5m])) by (cluster)
   - sum(rate(handoff_evicted_total[5m])) by (node)
2) Inspect dispatcher and node-agent dashboards: dispatcher.route_failures, node.queue_depth_p95, node.kv_sync_errors.
3) If a single node is overloaded: cordon it via node-agent API (dry-run first), allow existing handoffs to proceed, and unfavour new routing to it. Example API:
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -d '{"cordon": true, "eviction_window_secs": 60, "dry_run": true}' \
     https://runtime-node-agent.internal/v1/node/$NODE_ID/cordon
4) If topology-level saturation: scale up dedicated pools or adjust dispatcher routing policies to prefer fallback variants.
5) If KV sync errors: collect node-agent logs (tag: handoff.kv), and export traces from telemetry-service for the handoff_token.
6) Follow recovery verification checklist: handoff_commit_rate returns to baseline, handoff_evicted_total is flat, and canary synthetic workload p99 latency within expected tolerance.

Profiling and benchmarking guidance:
- Synthetic profiles to include in PRs changing handoff logic:
  * Short-request profile: 100k reqs, seq=64, concurrency=800. Report: handoff_commit_success, handoff_latency_p50/p95/p99.
  * Streamed-session profile: 3k sessions, avg_tokens=1500, concurrency=250. Report: kv_sync_success_rate, stream_handoff_commit_latency_p99.
- Profiling tips:
  - Correlate GPU kernel timeline (Nsight/trace) with handoff telemetry. Capture 2s samples across drain_epoch.
  - Sample node-agent state machine transitions and annotate traces with kernel ids to root-cause blockages.

Benchmark pass criteria for merge (non-exhaustive):
- handoff_success_rate >= 99.5% under 75% traffic;
- handoff_latency_p99 degradation <= 25% vs baseline;
- kv_sync_success_rate >= 98% for streaming workloads.

Release & rollout guidance:
- Any protocol change must publish a compatibility matrix and automated migration plan.
- Use feature-flagged canaries: 1% x24h, then 5% x48h, instrument both v1/v2 events.
- Provide explicit rollback actions: disable feature flag and allow existing tokens to expire over one eviction_window cycle.

Telemetry and SLOs (recommended):
- Metrics to emit: handoff_commit_total, handoff_evicted_total, handoff_reserve_timeout_total, handoff_kv_partial_total, handoff_latency_ms(quantiles), handoff_kv_sync_success_ratio.
- Example SLOs (hosted & dedicated):
  * Handoff commit success >= 99.5% monthly
  * User-visible aborts due to handoff <= 0.05% monthly
  * Handoff median latency <= 150ms, p99 <= 2.5s (non-stream workloads)

Debugging snippets:
- Node status (jq):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://runtime-node-agent.internal/v1/node/$NODE_ID/status | jq '.'
- Extract recent handoff traces via telemetry API:
  curl -s "https://telemetry-agent.internal/api/traces?tag=handoff_token&from=-10m" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq '.samples[] | {token: .token, events: .events}'
- Force a dry-run cordon (example):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"cordon": true, "eviction_window_secs": 45, "dry_run": true}' \
    https://runtime-node-agent.internal/v1/node/$NODE_ID/cordon

Owner and contacts:

- Primary engineers: Marissa Cheng (author), Andrej Kove1cs (handoff/orchestrator), Priya Raman (SRE lead)

Rollout checklist for protocol changes:
1) Unit tests + integration with simulated drain & blocked kernels.
2) PR-level synthetic benchmark comparisons saved to artifacts.
3) Canary rollout (1% -> 5%) with automated alert gates.
4) Full rollout with 30-minute pause windows between increments.
